⚡ You don't always need to build a power plant to make money from it.

Sometimes, the bigger opportunity is keeping it running.

That's where Power Mech Projects gets interesting.

The NSE-listed engineering company has just secured a ₹970 crore contract from Vedanta Power for end-to-end operations and maintenance of its 2×600 MW Sakti Thermal Power Plant in Chhattisgarh.

The contract runs for 60 months.

And this isn't an isolated project.

Power Mech says it manages 40+ GW of power-plant O&M globally, representing roughly 16% of India's thermal power base.

Its business has also expanded beyond traditional power construction into:

🏗️ Civil infrastructure
⚡ Power-plant O&M
🚆 Railways & metros
🛣️ Roads
💧 Water infrastructure
⛏️ Mining

The growth numbers are interesting too.

In Q1 FY27, revenue reached about ₹1,624 crore, up 26% YoY, while the company secured around ₹1,864 crore of new orders.

Its executable order book stood at approximately ₹16,229 crore, providing substantial revenue visibility.

What I find most interesting is the business model.

Building infrastructure creates one-time revenue.

Operating and maintaining that infrastructure can create long-duration revenue.

As India's power and infrastructure capacity expands, companies that can build, operate and maintain these assets could become increasingly important.

Is the real infrastructure opportunity sometimes in what happens AFTER construction is finished?

#PowerMechProjects #Infrastructure #PowerSector #IndiaGrowth #Engineering #Energy #Manufacturing #Business #NSE
comment: O&M businesses often get overlooked because they lack the visibility of new projects, but execution quality, uptime guarantees and cost efficiency become critical as assets age. The challenge is scaling expertise without compromising reliability.
